seed_case.note: Not counted in candidates_found (it is the seed, examined only to characterize the pattern, per task instructions). Its own 'what_would_make_this_wrong' text contains the exact self-admission language ('recovered from prior context rather than freshly read', 'own text ... cautions it has not verified against the original Step 155/156 artifacts') that no other record in the corpus reproduces verbatim -- see method note below.

method_note: Searched all 1793 records' what_says_this/what_would_make_this_wrong/notes_for_p3b fields for (1) exact-phrase signals ('recovered from prior context', 'not verified against', 'never checked against', 'self-admit', 'retrospective', 'reconstruct', 'summariz', 'restate', 'unverified', 'preview', 'own source', etc.), then (2) full-text manual review of every hit to judge whether the underlying provenance-asymmetry pattern (one side markedly less-verified/reconstructed vs. the other being the fuller, primary, verified record) was genuinely present, since 30 different batch-evaluators phrased this differently. Exact-phrase signals unique to RP0526 in the entire corpus: 'recovered from prior context' (1 hit, RP0526 only), 'not yet read'/'not freshly read' (1 hit, RP0526 only). Broader thematic buckets ('reconstruction' n=99, 'restate' n=97, 'preview' n=26, 'summariz' n=12, 'own source' n=26) were mostly false positives: 'reconstruction'/'preview' overwhelmingly name in-corpus research methodologies or draft-precedes-final maturity relationships (structurally different from RP0526's asymmetry), and the generic hedge phrase pattern 'would be wrong if X were independently/coincidentally derived' is standard boilerplate appearing in ~125 unrelated REFINEMENT/EXTENSION rows, not a marker of this specific pattern.

candidates_found.reasoning: Near-exact structural match to RP0526: a is explicitly characterized as 'the book's own chapter narrating and citing' the Constitution artifacts, 'a secondary narrative account built on b's already-established governance record', and 'a later narrative summary rather than the site where the governance gap was first found' -- a is a later, non-primary retelling of content b documents as the primary governance record. UNLIKE RP0526, this was classified conservatively as DERIVED-FROM, not SAME/REFINEMENT/EXTENSION. This is direct evidence that evaluators elsewhere in the corpus correctly downgrade this exact asymmetry rather than defaulting to a positive-continuity verdict.

A is explicitly the later document that 'incorporates/re-audits' b's specific finding as part of a broader re-review. The record's own what_would_make_this_wrong explicitly names the RP0526-shaped risk: 'If A's Section 5 re-audit merely cites/summarizes B's earlier finding without it being literally the same experimental result (e.g. an independent re-derivation reaching the same conclusion), this would be CORROBORATED-CONTINUATION rather than strict SAME.' The evaluator resolved this in favor of SAME on the strength of identical formulas/blocker language in both, which is somewhat stronger corroborating evidence than RP0526 had -- but the reasoning shape (a self-flagged 'could just be a summary' risk resolved toward a positive-continuity verdict) mirrors RP0526's structure closely enough to flag as the same risk pattern.

A is extracted directly from the primary source document (step-025g). B is explicitly 'later independent verification-pass restatements of that SAME document' drawn from separate audit/verification files, i.e. a secondary, downstream account rather than the primary artifact itself -- the same primary-vs-secondary shape as RP0526. Classified SAME (with an explicit recommendation to merge the labels). Weaker match than RP1470/RP0338 in one respect: b's secondary account is described as a verification/audit pass that reproduces the primary content 'near-verbatim' and even surfaces an internal contradiction in it, which is a stronger-verification act than RP0526's self-admittedly-unchecked retrospective recall -- so the asymmetry here is real but of a different, arguably safer, character than RP0526's.

B's own source (S1849) hedges that its D_t construct is 'not invented, but recovered from the corpus's own Zero-lens construction' -- an explicit self-admitted uncertainty about origin/directionality, structurally similar to RP0526's self-admitted-unverified caveat. The evaluator's own notes flag this: 'muddies directionality -- may be mutual/convergent rather than a clean one-way extension; flag for closer look.' Despite the flagged uncertainty, EXTENSION (a positive-continuity relationship) was still recorded, echoing RP0526's pattern of resolving a self-admitted provenance doubt in favor of the stronger relationship rather than the more conservative one.
